data.name: Gurjar
data.gender_notes: Gurjar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Gurjar is derived from the ancient Gurjar Kingdom in India. It is a term of respect and signifies a king or a ruler. The name Gurjar carries the meaning “King, Ruler” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Gurjar Kingdom in India tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Gurjar usually hope their child will grow to embody king, ruler and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Gurjar belongs to the Gurjar Kingdom in India linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “King, Ruler.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gurjar total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Gurjar carries the proud legacy of the brave and powerful Gurjar Kingdom of ancient India. It is associated with strength, valor, and leadership. Originally, it was used as a title bestowed upon kings and rulers. Today, it is continued to be used as a surname and a reminder of this rich cultural heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, the term 'Guru' means a teacher or a spiritual master who imparts wisdom and knowledge to his disciples. The name Gurjar carries a deeper spiritual significance as it is derived from the word 'Guru'. It is a reminder of the importance of the Guru in one's spiritual journey and the need to seek his guidance and blessings. It is also a reflection of the inner strength and wisdom that is required to become a true Guru or a spiritual teacher.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name 'Gurjar' is believed to originate from the Sanskrit word 'Gaj', meaning elephant, and the suffix '-raja', meaning king. Symbolically, it represents the inner strength and wisdom, resembling an elephant, coupled with the leadership and royalty of a king. This name is a reminder of one's innate power and authority, inspiring courage and confidence.
